title: Sam Butera and Chicago baritone with Frankie Duson
summary: Remarks on a young player later with Prima, his baritone playing in Chicago and work with Frankie Duson at the Pelican dance hall; a photograph is brought up.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Yeah. I'm trying to tell this little boy, those little boys that come here all the time. Uh, you got to pee pee funtin'. He's just come here all the time. Uh, you got to pee pee funtin'. Boy, and this boy right now is with a, with a, shit, I can't call him, he's a trumpet player, Prima, the tenor player. I can't call his name.
The tenor player with Prima? Yeah.

It used to be Sam Butera. Yeah, yeah, me, him too. Yeah. Yeah. Well, I can tell you some of the things I don't want to do, shit, make the headstand on the knee. I remember when I first went to Chicago, I used to play baritone too, you know. I used to play the hell out of baritone. I was small, skinny, and I was small. People never heard a baritone or something like that. No, I used to play the hell out of baritone. Okay. You used to play with Frankie Duesen, you were saying? On the Pelican? Yeah. Yeah? What was the Pelican? Huh? What was the Pelican? Oh, it was a nightclub like, huh? Yeah, a big dance hall. Oh, a big dance hall, I see. Was that fun? Huh? I played with so many guys, man. Man, I can't tell you. Yeah, I wanted to ask you about this picture here.
